beats.text: When you delete a file, your computer doesn't actually delete it.
At least, not on an old hard drive.
Deleting only removes the file's entry from the drive's index, like tearing a line out of a book's contents page.
The data itself is still sitting there. The space is just marked as free.
It stays until new files are written over it. That's how recovery tools bring files back.
And it's why selling an old hard drive without wiping it is risky.
Modern SSDs are different. When you delete, your computer sends a command called TRIM.
It tells the drive those blocks aren't needed, and the drive clears them in the background.
So on most new laptops, a deleted file can be truly gone within moments.
The lesson: on an old hard drive, delete isn't erase. On an SSD, delete is almost forever. Back up what matters.
